clue.text: Conservative, wise one, shows craft

parts.note: an oracle is a source of wise pronouncements, a sage

explanation.surface: A wise old Tory shows off his skill or cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill or cunning, but here it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker and hide, so a kind of watercraft.

clue.text: Moves stealthily and quietly among N American Indians

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Cree are a North American Indigenous people
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone slips stealthily and silently among Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and carefully so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Clara's upset by rogue

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Clara is distressed by a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, a scamp or rogue.

clue.text: Entrant in race scheming to crop time

indicators.note: scheming means plotting, so the letters are rearranged to a new plan

explanation.surface: A runner plots to cut down the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone entered in a contest or race is one of those competing in it.

clue.text: Player that offers more

definitions.meaning: a bit-part actor in a film crowd scene

explanation.definitionFit: A walk-on actor is a minor performer, and the same word means additional or over and above.

clue.text: There's no catch in it

parts.note: a body of water so salty that no fish live there, so an angler would land no catch

explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' reads as a hidden snag, but it means a haul of fish; this salt lake between Israel and Jordan supports no fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake's extreme salinity means no fish survive, so there is nothing to catch in it.

clue.text: Draughtsmen who've been overindulgent?

parts.note: draughtsmen read as people who take draughts, swigs of drink, to excess

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughtsmen' suggests technical artists or board-game pieces, but means drinkers of draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual heavy drinkers take too many draughts of alcohol.

clue.text: Part of influenza, chest pain

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Flu brings a pain in the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Oxford tie?

parts.note: an Oxford is a laced leather shoe, so its tie is the string that fastens it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford tie' suggests a university necktie, but an Oxford is a style of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord that fastens an Oxford shoe ties it, so it is the shoe's tie.

clue.text: German car, sort engineered for accounts people

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: engineered means rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German car of a certain type was engineered for bookkeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditors examine a firm's financial accounts professionally.

clue.text: Mopes around the course

indicators.note: around tells us to move the letters of mopes about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sulks gloomily about the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs is an English racecourse, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a famous horse-racing venue in Surrey, so it is a course in the racing sense.

clue.text: A charming utterance but it's inflammable

definitions.meaning: a phrase said like a charm to ward off bad luck
rotten wood dry enough to be used as tinder

explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' means acting as a lucky charm, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: People say the phrase superstitiously to avert misfortune, and the same word names punk or tinder that catches fire easily.

clue.text: Kitchen accessories, subsequently put into bundles

indicators.note: put into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: packs are bundles or parcels
later means subsequently, afterwards

explanation.surface: Kitchen items are afterwards tied up into bundles.
explanation.definitionFit: Racks for drying or storing dishes are standard fittings in a kitchen.

clue.text: Low-key dwelling?

definitions.meaning: subdued, lacking excitement; also, in music, lowered in pitch
a set of rooms on one floor, an apartment

explanation.definitionFit: A dull, subdued mood is described this way, and in Britain an apartment is called this too.

clue.text: Notice government official's conduct

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
a minister is a senior member of government

explanation.surface: Take note of how a government minister behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conduct' looks like a noun meaning behaviour but is the verb to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct affairs is to manage or run them, the same as administering them.

clue.text: One who makes it in the cinema world?

definitions.text: One who makes it in the cinema world?

parts.words: One who makes it in the cinema world?
parts.note: making it usually means succeeding, but here it is the thing that is made: a movie

explanation.walkthrough: 'makes it' looks like 'becomes a success'; read literally, 'it' is the picture being made.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who oversees the making of a movie literally makes it in the cinema business.

clue.text: Corrupt morals met in disorder

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Debased ethics were encountered amid chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool by extension means a scene of violent confusion and turmoil.

clue.text: About series of lessons, naturally

parts.note: of can mean about, as in to speak of something
a course is a programme of lessons

explanation.surface: Concerning a set of classes, it goes without saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means certainly, as expected, which is what naturally means as an interjection.

clue.text: Enclosed place that might be costlier

indicators.note: might be says these letters could become something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A walled-in site that could prove more expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered walkway enclosed within a monastery or college.

clue.text: Acted like others and kept up with court action

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from playing a card of the same suit, means imitating others; read literally it means tracking a lawsuit.

clue.text: Way a New Zealand article portrays verse

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A New Zealand newspaper piece depicts poetry in its own way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Tom let loose to become something on the ranch?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: let loose means set free, so those letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man named Tom is set free to become a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and steers are the livestock raised on a ranch.

clue.text: Newspaper's shortened deadline?

parts.note: a dead line: a few lines in the paper about someone who has died, given a clipped name

explanation.walkthrough: 'deadline' looks like a press time limit, but splits as 'dead line', a notice about the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form of obituary is a newspaper's death notice, and the word itself is abbreviated.

clue.text: Houseplant died with apiarists assembling netting

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so one piece goes within the other
assembling means putting the beekeepers' letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: A houseplant died while beekeepers gathered with nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' rearranges APIARISTS into ASPIISTRA, and 'netting' catches D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy plant traditionally kept indoors in parlours.

clue.text: I have written about area's statesman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a region's political leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' looks like a politician but reads as a man of a US state, here Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a US state is literally a state's man; this one comes from Iowa.

clue.text: In France I will precede the Queen, generating ridicule

indicators.note: will precede puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: je is French for I
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A French speaker goes before the monarch, provoking derision.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or ridicule loudly.

clue.text: Rank upon rank that's found running through Hyde Park

indicators.note: upon places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: rank in the sense of foul or putrid means rotten
a rank is a line of things side by side, a row

explanation.surface: Line after line of something is found running through a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London; this is the sandy riding track along its south side.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous bridleway lies along the south side of the London park, so it runs through it.

clue.text: Steadfast belief that's unaffected by a setback

indicators.note: a setback read as being turned back: reading the word backwards leaves it unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A firmly held conviction survives a reverse undamaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' sounds like a misfortune but means reading backwards; the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine held firmly is a central article of belief.

clue.text: One hears of a murder at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hears news of a killing on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanic membrane in the ear vibrates with sound, so it is the part that hears.

clue.text: Went quickly back to class to rehearse

indicators.note: back says the word for went quickly is read in reverse

parts.note: ran means went quickly
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone hurried back to a lesson to practise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rehearse' here means recount or relate, not practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a story in the older sense is to recount it in full, to tell it.
